title: After Uber, Moove leaves too: what it means for Lagos riders and drivers
excerpt: Two exits in five weeks have changed how people think about getting around Lagos. Here is what we know, what we do not, and what to ask of any service you use.
body:
## Two announcements, one question

In September 2026 Uber confirmed it would leave Nigeria. In early October the vehicle financier Moove, a partner of Uber, reported that it was ending its Nigerian operations and transferring vehicles worth about ₦35 billion to its customers. Both stories are covered in the sources below.

## What this does not tell us

These are company decisions. They do not mean Lagos stops moving. Riders and drivers are still choosing between other apps, scheduled services and professional transfers.

## What riders can ask of any service

- **A fare you can see before you confirm.** Surprise pricing is the main complaint riders raise.
- **Drivers who are checked.** Ask what ID, licence and background checks are done.
- **Clear cancellation rules.** Know the refund rule before you pay.
- **A person to call.** A real support line matters when a trip goes wrong.

## What drivers can ask

- **A transparent share of each fare.** Drivers in Lagos have publicly asked for lower commission and better terms.
- **Safe tools.** An emergency button, trip records and verified riders.
- **A route to grow.** Training, better trips and honest communication.

## Where RideArrivo fits

RideArrivo focuses on Lagos airport pickups, scheduled rides, chauffeur, and moves and charter, with the fare shown up front and drivers who are verified. See [every RideArrivo service](/#services) and the [driver side](/drivers).
